action: Prescribe chronic anticoagulant therapy for HF patients with AF and elevated CHA2DS2-VASc score
action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >=2 (men) or >=3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention
source_text: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (for men) and >= 3 (for women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Prescribe DOAC over Warfarin for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF and permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. DOACs have fixed dosing, fewer drug-drug interactions, and no need for routine anticoagulation monitoring. In meta-analysis, DOACs more effectively reduced stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin.

properties.context: preferred over warfarin in HF patients

source_text: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs in the polypharmacy setting of HF
action_detail: The guideline notes that DOACs have fewer drug-drug interactions than warfarin, which simplifies management in HF patients who typically require polypharmacy (beta blockers, ACEi/ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, diuretics, amiodarone, digoxin). Warfarin's narrow therapeutic index and CYP2C9/VKORC1-mediated metabolism make it susceptible to interactions with amiodarone, which is commonly used for AF rhythm control in HF. Warfarin may still be preferred when DOAC interactions or cost are concerns.

properties.mechanism: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs due to CYP-mediated metabolism and narrow therapeutic index
properties.clinical_effect: DOACs preferred due to fewer interactions in polypharmacy HF setting
properties.management: Consider DOAC over warfarin; if warfarin chosen, monitor INR closely especially with concomitant amiodarone or other CYP inhibitors

source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF (Class I, LOE A)

action: Warfarin interacts with Amiodarone requiring dose adjustment and closer INR monitoring
action_detail: The guideline discusses amiodarone as a rhythm control agent for AF in HF (AATAC trial) and separately notes warfarin's susceptibility to drug-drug interactions as a reason to prefer DOACs. Amiodarone is a potent CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor that increases warfarin levels by 30-50%, raising bleeding risk. When both are co-prescribed in HF+AF patients, warfarin dose should be reduced by 30-50% and INR monitored more frequently.

properties.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, reducing warfarin metabolism and increasing anticoagulant effect
properties.clinical_effect: Increased INR and bleeding risk; warfarin levels increase 30-50%
properties.management: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% when initiating amiodarone; increase INR monitoring frequency

source_text: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions (the DOAC are generally preferred)

action: Warfarin interacts with Digoxin requiring monitoring
action_detail: In HF patients with AF requiring both rate control (digoxin) and anticoagulation (warfarin), the two drugs may interact. Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index and warfarin-digoxin co-administration may modestly alter digoxin clearance. More importantly, both drugs require careful monitoring in the polypharmacy HF setting the guideline describes. The guideline's preference for DOAC over warfarin partly reflects the complexity of managing warfarin alongside other HF medications including digoxin.

properties.mechanism: Both have narrow therapeutic indices; co-administration in polypharmacy HF setting increases monitoring burden
properties.clinical_effect: Increased complexity of anticoagulation management; potential for altered digoxin or warfarin levels
properties.management: Monitor INR and digoxin levels; consider DOAC instead of warfarin to simplify regimen

source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF

action: AF ablation is reasonable for symptom improvement in HF patients
action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, catheter ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and quality of life. In AATAC trial (persistent AF, LVEF <40%, NYHA II-III), ablation improved sinus rhythm maintenance vs amiodarone with 45% decrease in hospitalization and lower mortality. In CASTLE-AF trial (AF, LVEF <35%, NYHA II-IV), ablation reduced composite of death/rehospitalization (28.5% vs 44.6%).

properties.context: in HF patients with AF-related symptoms

source_text: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation is reasonable when rhythm/rate control fails in AF with LVEF <=50%
action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <=50%, if rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. CRT produced more benefit than RV pacing in trials (PAVE, BLOCK-HF).

properties.context: after AV nodal ablation when rate/rhythm control fails, LVEF <=50%

source_text: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if a rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired, and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, AV nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor INR for warfarin therapy in HF patients with AF
action_detail: When warfarin is used for anticoagulation in HF patients with AF (when favored because of other indications, cost, or drug-drug interactions), routine anticoagulation monitoring with INR is required. Therapeutic INR range is 2.0-3.0. This is implied by the guideline contrasting DOACs (which do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring) with warfarin.
source_text: These drugs [DOACs] do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment... Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions.

action: Consider AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation when rhythm control fails in AF with LVEF <=50%
action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <=50%, if rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. CRT is preferred over RV pacing in patients with reduced LVEF.
source_text: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if a rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired, and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: Use specific DOAC agents for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: Several DOACs are available including factor Xa inhibitors apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran. In meta-analysis of 4 trials, DOACs more effectively reduced stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin, with no treatment heterogeneity by HF status.
source_text: Several DOAC are available, including the factor Xa inhibitors apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and the direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran... DOAC more effectively reduced the rate of stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin.

action: Do not administer ARNi to patients with history of angioedema
action_detail: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema due to the concern that it will increase the risk of recurrence. Angioedema was an exclusion criterion in PARADIGM-HF. Rates of angioedema were numerically higher with ARNi vs ACEi.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. (Class III: Harm, LOE C-LD)

action: Do not administer ACEi to patients with history of angioedema
action_detail: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. Angioedema attributable to ACEi results from defective degradation of bradykinin, des-Arg9-BK, and substance P. ARB may be used as an alternative as they do not interfere as directly with bradykinin metabolism.
source_text: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. (Class III: Harm, LOE C-LD)

action: Do not administer ARNi concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of last ACEi dose
action_detail: Oral neprilysin inhibitors combined with ACEi can lead to angioedema. Both ACEi and neprilysin break down bradykinin, and dual inhibition causes unacceptable incidence of angioedema. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching between ACEi and ARNi.

properties.mechanism: dual bradykinin degradation inhibition causing angioedema risk

source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer ARNi concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi
action_detail: Concomitant use of ARNi with ACEi is contraindicated due to risk of angioedema from dual inhibition of neprilysin and ACE pathways, both of which degrade bradykinin. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching between ACEi and ARNi.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last ACEi dose
action_detail: Sacubitril/Valsartan (the only approved ARNi) must not be given with any ACEi. Omapatrilat (a combined neprilysin/ACE inhibitor) showed unacceptable angioedema rates in RCTs, leading to its development termination. The mechanism involves dual inhibition of bradykinin degradation by both ACE and neprilysin pathways.
source_text: Oral neprilysin inhibitors, used in combination with ACEi, can lead to angioedema, and concomitant use is contraindicated. An ARNi should not be administered within 36 hours of switching from or to an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan with Enalapril
action_detail: In PARADIGM-HF, sacubitril/valsartan was compared with enalapril. Concomitant use of neprilysin inhibitors with ACEi leads to angioedema via dual bradykinin pathway inhibition. A 36-hour washout is required when switching between these agents.
source_text: Oral neprilysin inhibitors, used in combination with ACEi, can lead to angioedema, and concomitant use is contraindicated and should be avoided. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan with Lisinopril
action_detail: Concomitant use of ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan) with any ACEi including lisinopril is contraindicated due to angioedema risk from dual bradykinin pathway inhibition. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan with Ramipril
action_detail: Concomitant use of ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan) with any ACEi including ramipril is contraindicated due to angioedema risk from dual bradykinin pathway inhibition. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan with Captopril
action_detail: Concomitant use of ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan) with any ACEi including captopril is contraindicated due to angioedema risk from dual bradykinin pathway inhibition. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor potassium after MRA initiation
action_detail: Careful monitoring of serum potassium should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia. Check at approximately 1 week, then 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiating or intensifying MRA, with more frequent testing for clinical instability.
source_text: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency (Class I, LOE A)

action: Monitor renal function after MRA initiation
action_detail: Regular checks of renal function should be performed approximately 1 week, then 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiating or intensifying MRA, with more frequent testing for clinical instability. eGFR must be >30 mL/min/1.73m2 before initiation.
source_text: Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed according to clinical status, approximately 1 week, then 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiating or intensifying MRA

action: Monitor potassium with spironolactone therapy
action_detail: Spironolactone decreases renal potassium excretion, raising the risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium at 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months. Do not initiate if potassium >=5.0 mEq/L. Discontinue if potassium cannot be maintained <5.5 mEq/L.
source_text: Spironolactone and eplerenone decrease renal potassium excretion, raising the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly when MRA is initiated at serum potassium >=5.0 mEq/L and continued >=5.5 mEq/L

action: Monitor potassium with eplerenone therapy
action_detail: Eplerenone decreases renal potassium excretion, raising the risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium at 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months. Do not initiate if potassium >=5.0 mEq/L. Discontinue if potassium cannot be maintained <5.5 mEq/L.
source_text: Spironolactone and eplerenone decrease renal potassium excretion, raising the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly when MRA is initiated at serum potassium >=5.0 mEq/L and continued >=5.5 mEq/L

action: Prescribe MRA for HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II to IV symptoms, an MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone) is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality, if eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73m2 and serum potassium <5.0 mEq/L.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II to IV symptoms, an MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone) is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality, if eGFR is >30 mL/min/1.73m2 and serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L (Class I, LOE A)

action: Discontinue MRA if potassium cannot be maintained below 5.5 mEq/L
action_detail: In patients taking MRA whose serum potassium cannot be maintained at <5.5 mEq/L, MRA should be discontinued to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia. This is a Class III (Harm) recommendation.
source_text: In patients taking MRA whose serum potassium cannot be maintained at <5.5 mEq/L, MRA should be discontinued to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia (Class III Harm, LOE B-NR)

action: Start spironolactone at 25 mg daily, titrate to 50 mg daily
action_detail: Starting dose of spironolactone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month. For eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, dosing should be reduced by half (start 12.5 mg daily).
source_text: The starting dose of spironolactone and eplerenone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month; for eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, dosing should be reduced by half

action: Start eplerenone at 25 mg daily, titrate to 50 mg daily
action_detail: Starting dose of eplerenone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month. For eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, dosing should be reduced by half (start 12.5 mg daily).
source_text: The starting dose of spironolactone and eplerenone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month; for eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, dosing should be reduced by half

action: Do not initiate MRA if eGFR <=30 or potassium >=5.0
action_detail: eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2 or serum potassium >=5.0 mEq/L are contraindications to MRA initiation. Spironolactone and eplerenone are partially excreted through the kidneys, raising concerns about safety when eGFR is <=30.
source_text: eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2 or serum potassium >=5.0 mEq/L are contraindications to MRA initiation

action: Coadministration of MRA with ACEi or ARB mildly increases hyperkalemia risk
action_detail: Coadministration of MRA with ACEi or ARB mildly increases the risk of hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia risk was lower with ARNi compared with ACEi in chronic HF (PARADIGM-HF). Monitor potassium more closely when combining these agents.
source_text: Coadministration of MRA with ACEi or ARB mildly increases the risk of hyperkalemia

action: Coadministration of MRA with ARB mildly increases hyperkalemia risk
action_detail: Coadministration of MRA with ARB mildly increases the risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium more closely when combining these agents.
source_text: Coadministration of MRA with ACEi or ARB mildly increases the risk of hyperkalemia

action: Consider temporarily holding MRA during dehydration or loop diuretic interruption
action_detail: Diarrhea causing dehydration or loop diuretic therapy interruption, because of worsening renal function or hyperkalemia, should be a consideration for temporarily holding the MRA. The development of worsening renal function or hyperkalemia is often a reflection of acute clinical change.
source_text: Diarrhea causing dehydration or loop diuretic therapy interruption, because of worsening renal function or hyperkalemia, should be a consideration for temporarily holding the MRA

action: Monitor renal function with spironolactone therapy
action_detail: Spironolactone is partially excreted through the kidneys. Monitor eGFR at 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiation. Do not initiate if eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2. Reduce dose by half for eGFR 31-49 mL/min/1.73m2.
source_text: Spironolactone and eplerenone are partially excreted through the kidneys, raising concerns about safety when eGFR is <=30 mL/min/1.73m2

action: Monitor renal function with eplerenone therapy
action_detail: Eplerenone is partially excreted through the kidneys. Monitor eGFR at 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiation. Do not initiate if eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2. Reduce dose by half for eGFR 31-49 mL/min/1.73m2.
source_text: Spironolactone and eplerenone are partially excreted through the kidneys, raising concerns about safety when eGFR is <=30 mL/min/1.73m2

action: Increase monitoring frequency for MRA during clinical instability
action_detail: More frequent testing of potassium and renal function should be performed during clinical instability, beyond the standard schedule of 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months. Worsening renal function or hyperkalemia often reflects acute clinical change or progressive disease.
source_text: Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed according to clinical status...with more frequent testing for clinical instability

action: Do not use nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem and verapamil) are not recommended. They are myocardial depressants with negative inotropic effects. Diltiazem was associated with higher risk of recurrent HF after acute MI. Verapamil had no survival benefit post-MI including in HFrEF.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended. (Class 3: Harm, LOE A)

action: Do not use vitamins, nutritional supplements, or hormonal therapy for HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and hormonal therapy are not recommended other than to correct specific deficiencies. No benefit demonstrated for vitamin D, thiamine, carnitine, taurine. Potential harm from vitamin E. Coenzyme Q10 showed mixed results. Testosterone, growth hormone, and thyroid hormone showed neutral effects.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and hormonal therapy are not recommended other than to correct specific deficiencies. (Class 3: No Benefit, LOE B-R)

action: Avoid class IC antiarrhythmic medications and dronedarone in HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications (encainide, flecainide) and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. CAST trial showed increased mortality with encainide/flecainide post-MI. ANDROMEDA trial showed increased mortality with dronedarone in hospitalized HFrEF. SWORD trial showed increased mortality with sotalol post-MI HF. Amiodarone and dofetilide are the only antiarrhythmics with neutral mortality effects in HFrEF.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. (Class 3: Harm, LOE A)

action: Avoid DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin in patients with HF
action_detail: In patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, the DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. FDA recommends discontinuation of saxagliptin and alogliptin in patients who develop HF. Sitagliptin and linagliptin did not show this risk. Whether this is a class effect is unclear.
source_text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, the DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. (Class 3: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Avoid NSAIDs in patients with HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandin synthesis, causing sodium and water retention and blunting the effects of diuretics. Both nonselective and selective NSAIDs (COX-2 inhibitors) are associated with increased morbidity and mortality in HF.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. (Class 3: Harm, LOE B-NR)

action: Monitor serum digoxin concentration to maintain below 1.2 ng/mL
action_detail: Retrospective analyses of large-scale clinical trials showed a linear relationship between mortality and digoxin serum concentration. Risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with significantly higher risk at concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL. This threshold is clinically critical when digoxin is co-administered with drugs that raise serum digoxin levels (e.g., amiodarone).
source_text: The risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with a significantly higher risk observed in those with concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL.

action: Use caution when withdrawing digoxin
action_detail: Clinical worsening after withdrawal of digoxin has been shown. Therapy with digoxin may either be continued in the absence of a contraindication or discontinued with caution. Abrupt withdrawal may lead to clinical deterioration.
source_text: Clinical worsening after withdrawal of digoxin has been shown. Therapy with digoxin may either be continued in the absence of a contraindication or discontinued with caution.

action: Reduce digoxin dose in elderly, renal impairment, or low lean body mass
action_detail: Low doses of digoxin (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass. These conditions reduce digoxin clearance and increase toxicity risk, which is particularly relevant when combined with drugs that raise serum digoxin concentration.

properties.dose_adjustment: 0.125 mg daily or every other day
properties.indication: age >70, renal impairment, low lean body mass

source_text: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass.

action: Consider digoxin in symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT
action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. The benefit of digoxin in patients with HF remains controversial. GDMT is expected to be optimized before considering addition of digoxin.
source_text: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. (Class 2b, LOE B-R)

action: Consider ivabradine for symptomatic HFrEF with heart rate >=70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta blocker
action_detail: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II-III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <=35%) receiving GDMT including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate >=70 bpm, ivabradine can be beneficial to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular death

properties.context: add-on when HR >=70 bpm on max beta blocker

source_text: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II to III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <= 35%) who are receiving GDMT, including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, and who are in sinus rhythm with a heart rate of >= 70 bpm at rest, ivabradine can be beneficial (COR 2a, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor renal function during digoxin therapy
action_detail: Digoxin is renally cleared. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used if the patient has impaired renal function. Monitor eGFR and creatinine to guide dose adjustments and prevent digoxin accumulation and toxicity.

properties.reason: digoxin is renally cleared; impaired renal function increases toxicity risk
digoxin is renally cleared; monitor creatinine for dose adjustment

source_text: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass.

action: Monitor potassium during digoxin therapy
action_detail: Electrolyte monitoring, particularly potassium, is important during digoxin therapy. Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity by enhancing binding of digoxin to the sodium-potassium ATPase. Maintain potassium in normal range (3.5-5.0 mEq/L) to reduce toxicity risk.
source_text: Digoxin is usually initiated at a low dose because higher doses are rarely required in the management of HF and are potentially detrimental. Risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration.

action: Consider vericiguat for high-risk HFrEF with recent worsening
action_detail: In selected high-risk patients with HFrEF and recent worsening of HF already on GDMT, oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (vericiguat) may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death. Patients should have LVEF <45%, NYHA II-IV, elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP >=300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >=1000 pg/mL in sinus rhythm), and recent HF worsening.
source_text: In selected high-risk patients with HFrEF and recent worsening of HF already on GDMT, an oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (vericiguat) may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death (COR 2b, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor natriuretic peptides to assess eligibility for vericiguat
action_detail: Patients considered for vericiguat should have elevated natriuretic peptides: BNP >=300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >=1000 pg/mL if in sinus rhythm (higher cutoffs with atrial fibrillation). Patients in the highest quartile of NT-proBNP (>5314 pg/mL) did not benefit from vericiguat.
source_text: Patients with HFrEF in the VICTORIA trial had LVEF <45%, NYHA class II to IV, were on GDMT, with elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP >= 300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >= 1000 pg/mL if in sinus rhythm; higher cutoffs with AF)

action: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs in HF patients on polypharmacy
action_detail: Warfarin requires routine anticoagulation monitoring and dose adjustment, and has more drug-drug interactions compared with DOACs. The polypharmacy commonly seen in HF increases the clinical significance of warfarin interactions. When warfarin is used (due to cost, other indications, or patient factors), clinicians should be aware of interaction potential with other HF medications. DOACs are generally preferred due to fewer interactions.
source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF...Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions

action: Anticoagulate HF patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc score >= 2 (men) or >= 3 (women)
action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (for men) and >= 3 (for women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention. This applies regardless of whether patients receive rhythm or rate control.
source_text: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (men) and >= 3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy (Class I, LOE A)

action: AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms in HF patients with symptomatic AF
action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and quality of life. In AATAC trial, ablation improved maintenance of sinus rhythm compared with amiodarone, with 45% decrease in hospitalization and decrease in mortality. In CASTLE AF, the composite endpoint of death or rehospitalization was lower with ablation (28.5%) compared with standard care (44.6%).

properties.context: preferred over amiodarone for rhythm control in HF

source_text: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL (Class IIa, LOE B-R). Ablation versus amiodarone: AATAC showed 45% decrease in hospitalization and decreased mortality

action: Use warfarin instead of DOAC when drug-drug interactions favor warfarin monitoring
action_detail: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost, or drug-drug interactions. While DOAC is generally preferred, warfarin may be chosen when its INR monitoring enables safer management of known drug-drug interactions (e.g., with amiodarone, which can be titrated based on INR). This is particularly relevant in HF patients on antiarrhythmics.
source_text: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions (the DOAC are generally preferred)

action: Assess CHA2DS2-VASc score before initiating anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: Use CHA2DS2-VASc score to assess patient risk for adverse outcomes before initiating anticoagulation therapy. Anticoagulation is recommended for CHA2DS2-VASc score >=2 (men) and >=3 (women). Score components: hypertension, age >=75 (doubled), diabetes, prior stroke/TIA/thromboembolism (doubled), vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category.
source_text: The AHA/ACC/Heart Rhythm Society guidelines for AF recommend use of the CHA2DS2-VASc score to assess patient risk for adverse outcomes before initiating anticoagulation therapy (COR 1, LOE A).

action: Prefer DOAC over warfarin for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients with HF and AF. DOACs include apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and dabigatran. DOACs more effectively reduced stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin. Warfarin may be favored for other indications, cost, or drug-drug interactions.
source_text: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients (COR 1, LOE A). DOACs do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment.

action: DOACs do not require routine anticoagulation monitoring
action_detail: Unlike warfarin, DOACs (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran) do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment. The fixed dosing together with fewer drug interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with polypharmacy commonly seen in HF.
source_text: These drugs do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment. The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF.

action: AV nodal ablation with CRT device implantation for refractory rapid AF in HF
action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <=50%, if rhythm control fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, AV nodal ablation with CRT device implantation is reasonable. CRT is preferred over RV pacing based on PAVE and BLOCK-HF trials.
source_text: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if a rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired, and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, AV nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable (COR 2a, LOE B-R).

action: Monitor heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, renal function, and symptoms during GDMT uptitration
action_detail: Patients should be monitored for changes in heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, renal function, and symptoms during the uptitration period of ACEi, ARB, ARNi, and other GDMT. Planned uptitration should be delayed until any adverse effects observed with lower doses have resolved.
source_text: Patients should be monitored for changes in heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, renal function, and symptoms during this uptitration period. (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor renal function and serum potassium during ACEi therapy
action_detail: ACEi should be given with caution to patients with renal insufficiency or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). Renal function and electrolytes should be checked at initiation, during uptitration, and periodically thereafter.
source_text: ACEi should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressures, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor renal function and serum potassium during ARB therapy
action_detail: ARB should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). Renal function and electrolytes should be checked at initiation, during uptitration, and periodically thereafter.
source_text: ARB should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor renal function, potassium, and blood pressure during ARNi therapy
action_detail: ARNi use is more frequently associated with symptomatic hypotension. Monitor renal function (worsening renal function), hyperkalemia, and symptomatic hypotension. In PIONEER-HF, ARNi did not increase rates of worsening renal function, hyperkalemia, or symptomatic hypotension compared with enalapril.
source_text: PIONEER-HF showed ARNi reduced NT-proBNP without increased rates of worsening renal function, hyperkalemia, symptomatic hypotension, angioedema compared with enalapril. (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor potassium and renal function during MRA therapy with specific timing schedule
action_detail: Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed approximately 1 week after initiation, then 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiating or intensifying MRA, with more frequent testing for clinical instability. MRA should not be initiated if eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2 or potassium >=5.0 mEq/L.
source_text: Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed approximately 1 week, then 4 weeks, then every 3 months after initiating or intensifying MRA. (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Discontinue MRA if serum potassium cannot be maintained below 5.5 mEq/L
action_detail: In patients taking MRA whose serum potassium cannot be maintained at <5.5 mEq/L, MRA should be discontinued to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia.
source_text: In patients taking MRA whose serum potassium cannot be maintained at <5.5 mEq/L, MRA should be discontinued to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia. (COR 3: Harm, LOE B-NR)

action: Uptitrate GDMT as frequently as every 1 to 2 weeks guided by symptoms, vital signs, and laboratory findings
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, titration and optimization of guideline-directed medications as frequently as every 1 to 2 weeks depending on the patient's symptoms, vital signs, and laboratory findings (including electrolytes and renal function) can be useful to optimize management.
source_text: Titration and optimization of GDMT as frequently as every 1 to 2 weeks depending on patient's symptoms, vital signs, and laboratory findings can be useful to optimize management. (COR 2a, LOE C-EO)

action: Monitor for hyperkalemia risk when MRA is co-administered with ACEi or ARB
action_detail: Coadministration of MRA with ACEi or ARB mildly increases the risk of hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia risk was lower with ARNi compared to ACEi in PARADIGM-HF but not different in PIONEER-HF. Monitor potassium closely when combining RAS inhibitors with MRA.

increased risk when combined with MRA

action: Monitor blood pressure during ACEi and ARNi therapy for symptomatic hypotension
action_detail: ACEi should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressures. ARNi use is more frequently associated with symptomatic hypotension compared with enalapril. Blood pressure should be monitored at each visit and during uptitration.
source_text: ACEi should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressures. ARNi use is more frequently associated with symptomatic hypotension compared with enalapril. (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor renal function and potassium during MRA dose adjustment for reduced eGFR
action_detail: For patients with eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, MRA dosing should be reduced by half (spironolactone 12.5 mg daily, eplerenone 12.5 mg daily). Close monitoring of renal function and potassium is required in this population.
source_text: For eGFR 31 to 49 mL/min/1.73m2, dosing should be reduced by half. Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed. (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor potassium at MRA initiation and closely thereafter
action_detail: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency
source_text: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency (COR 1, LOE A)

action: Monitor creatinine during MRA therapy

action: Monitor for genitourinary infections and ketoacidosis during SGLT2i therapy
action_detail: Caution is warranted for euglycemic ketoacidosis, genital and soft tissue infections, and adjustment of diuretics if needed to prevent volume depletion during SGLT2i therapy
source_text: As the use of SGLT2i is translated into clinical practice, caution is warranted for euglycemic ketoacidosis, genital and soft tissue infections, and adjustment of diuretics, if needed, to prevent volume depletion

action: Monitor eGFR decline during SGLT2i therapy
action_detail: In DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced trials, serious renal outcomes were less frequent and rate of decline in eGFR was slower in patients treated with SGLT2i. eGFR monitoring should continue during therapy

action: Monitor potassium and renal function for MRA in HFpEF
action_detail: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing at initiation and follow-up are key to minimizing the risk of hyperkalemia and worsening renal function in patients with HFpEF on spironolactone
source_text: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing at initiation and follow-up are key to minimizing the risk of hyperkalemia and worsening renal function (TOPCAT, HFpEF)

action: MRA dose adjustment for reduced eGFR
action_detail: Starting dose of spironolactone and eplerenone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month. For eGFR 31-49 mL/min/1.73 m2, dosing should be reduced by half

action: Monitor for genitourinary infections during SGLT2i therapy in HFrEF with diabetes
action_detail: Patients on SGLT2i should be closely monitored for potential risks, including severe genitourinary infections and, less commonly, diabetic ketoacidosis

action: Initiate digoxin at 0.125-0.25 mg daily
action_detail: Digoxin is usually initiated at a low dose (0.125-0.25 mg daily) because higher doses are rarely required and are potentially detrimental. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used if patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has low lean body mass. Higher doses (0.375-0.50 mg daily) are rarely used or needed.
